description: Highly sought variegated aroid, mass-propagated in vitro. Buyers go TC for cheap access to the cream/green splash — but variegation stability varies by lab and deflasking is the make-or-break step.
The lab-stable variegated Monstera — creamy galaxy speckling that (unlike albo) doesn't revert. Slow in vitro, so expect fewer plantlets per cup and a premium price.
Velvety heart-shaped leaves with bright white venation. TC gives pest-free, uniform stock — but clarinervium plantlets are humidity-fussy and unforgiving to deflask for beginners.
Fast, forgiving arrowhead vine with green-and-cream variegation. One of the easier TC plants to deflask — high plantlet counts per cup make it a great first tissue-culture buy.
Dark velvet leaves with white venation and splashed variegation. Alocasia are notoriously hard to acclimate out of flask — later-stage cups from a proven lab are worth the premium here.
Fragrant species orchid, almost always started in flask. Orchid seedlings are slow and sold as community pots or deflasked compots — a low-contamination lab matters more than raw plantlet count.
Spiralled silver-and-plum rex begonia. Propagates prolifically in vitro (high plantlet counts) but the thin leaves resent low humidity right after deflasking.
The coveted pink-variegated aroid. TC plantlets can carry unstable pink that reverts — phenotype_stability and a lab that culls reverting stock are everything for this one.

One of the rarest philodendrons on earth — long, pendant, arrow-shaped leaves. TC is the only way it ever comes cheap, but plantlets are slow and precious, so a proven low-contamination lab matters far more than plantlet count.

The famous 'more hole than leaf' aroid, endlessly confused with adansonii. Paper-thin runners are fragile out of flask — later-stage, well-rooted plantlets survive acclimation far better than raw cups.

The Queen anthurium — long, pendulous velvet leaves with silver venation. Notoriously slow and humidity-hungry from flask; deflask success separates the labs, and cheap in-vitro cups are a beginner heartbreak.

Dark stems with bold white-blocked leaves. Like other white-variegated aroids the variegation can revert or fry, so phenotype stability and a lab that culls unstable stock decide whether your plantlet keeps its splash.

Silvery-green leaves embossed like reptile scales. A jewel alocasia that sulks and drops leaves at the smallest humidity swing — acclimated, hardened-off plants from a trusted lab dodge the classic deflasking meltdown.

The variegated 'mini monstera' — fast-growing split leaves splashed with cream. Vigorous and forgiving for a variegate, so high plantlet counts per cup make it one of the more rewarding TC buys once deflasked.

The curled 'Hindu rope' wax plant — thick, waxy, drought-tolerant leaves. One of the toughest TC plants to establish and slow but near-indestructible once out, making high-count cups a low-risk beginner tissue-culture buy.

A ground-clustering tropical pitcher plant, almost always mass-propagated in flask. Seedlings want high humidity and pure water out of the cup — a low-contamination lab beats raw plantlet count for carnivores.
